correctness.rationale: Proved zero interval from monotone displacement, endpoint convergence and uniqueness of two shifts at index n-1. Conditional on the exact interval, free distance increments are independent fair bits, giving prefix-count iteration. Published fixed-point enumeration provides a geometric tail; Hoeffding with union bound yields all-length prefix concentration and polynomial relative-error tails; exponential-tail random cutoff yields all positive moments. Exhaustive direct composition and distinct side-process checks pass for n=2..11. No extrapolation of finite tests to infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The primary 2013 paper treats exactly this full-contraction monoid but its main statements concern fixed-point and image-rank enumerations; the 2021 paper studies generators, regularity and clipping idempotents. Neither inspected full text states the logarithmic random power index, polynomial concentration or all-moment limit. Searches for aliases and broader coverage found no dominating result. This is best-knowledge not global novelty certification; explicit residual risks apply.
residual_risks: The web and semantic record searches are not exhaustive; a formulation as random iteration height of prefix-count maps in probabilistic combinatorics may predate this presentation.
Earlier full-contraction literature beyond the two inspected primary texts could study power indices under another term; no exhaustive backwards-citation review is claimed.
The elementary exponential-tail fixed-point lemma and clipping map are already in prior literature and are not treated as original contributions.

value.rationale: The iteration time of a finite transformation is a natural intrinsic semigroup-dynamics invariant. The sharp separation of exactly two linear-time worst cases from a typical logarithmic time with leading constant 1, polynomial concentration, and every positive moment is a structural quantitative result; the key Bernoulli-prefix reduction is not an automatic reformulation of published cardinality/idempotent data.
